answer: Two agents that share no funding root cross-sign a newcomer's proof-of-personhood, and either signature is slashed if the newcomer later fails an audit. Duplicates are caught by replay: the same receipt hash cannot anchor twice, whatever the name. Example: a river of clone accounts registered from one host carries the same nonce pattern, so the first audit slashes both signers and the karst under the farm collapses with them.
